chapter: Hines 1935-38, Gus Arnheim and Billy Eckstine
title: Eckstine at Club DeLisa; "you can't quit" the mob
summary: Fox rejects Eckstine, who takes a job at Mike DeLisa's, where Budd says nobody was allowed to quit and Scatman Crothers was beaten for leaving.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Well, I'm trying to get in with Earl's band, and we're trying to convince Ed Fox. Ed Fox say, "Aw, that bum can't sing." I said, "Man, he can sing, man." He says, "Don't need him. I got Leroy Harris." Leroy was singing in the band at that time.
So, Billy got a job at -- at Club Delisa. That is, you know --
Yeah.
-- the one that burned down over on State Street.
That was on State Street on the -- on the west side of State Street.
That's right. On the west side of
State Street.
Albert Ammons used to play there, right?
Yeah. That's right. Albert Ammons. Oh, man.
Guy Kelly was in the band over there.

Yeah. Alvin Burroughs and all of these cats. And, this was -- this was a place, a night club, where you had a floor show and a -- and a good little band up there. Then, this is when I met Leon Washington, the tenor saxophone player.
That's right. He was with --

And, you could get a spaghetti dinner for 15 cents and see a floor show, and you drank your beer for a dime. So, Billy Ekstein got this job at Mike DeLisa's. And, while he was waiting to try to join Earl's band. So, finally, I convinced them to get Billy Ekstein.
Billy had to beg Mike to let him quit, because, you know, they -- they didn't let nobody quit. No, you just -- worked for
(Inaudible.) ... the mob.

No, you couldn't quit. Because, I remember when Spo-De-O-Dee came there from St. Louis and these cats got on the train and came there and went into the Mike DeLisa's and beat the hell out of Spo-De-O-De.
and took him back to St. Louis where he was working in the Plantation there and says, "You quit when we tell you you can quit. You don't leave us."
-- everybody know who Sco-be-o-De is, he's the little friend of Louis who wrote "I'll be Glad when You're Dead, You Rascal You" for Louie.
That's right.
I just wanted --
A beautiful man. Great in show business back in those days.
Great comedian.
